newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: GM says Opel/Vauxhall 1996 profit falls 2.3 percent.
newsitem.headline: GM says Opel/Vauxhall 1996 profit falls 2.3 percent.

text.p: General Motors Europe, the international division of the automotive giant, said Tuesday that 1996 net profits at its Opel/Vauxhall unit eased to $778 million from 1995's $796 million.
Richard Donnelly, GM Europe president, said in a statement that investments in Europe this year were expected to rise by around 15 percent to almost $1.9 billion from 1995's $1.65 billion.
"High investments in new product programmes and new plants continue to be an expression of our confidence in the future of the automobile business in Europe," GM said.
GM Europe also said that GM's International Operations, which comprise its units outside the United States, Canada and Mexico, had 1996 sales of $35.25 billion and net profit of $1.53 billion.
In 1996 Opel/Vauxhall recorded an operating profit of $1.02 billion in its core car and light commercial vehicle business on record sales revenue of $25.53 billion, up from 1995's $24.94 billion.
It added that the technically identical Opel/Vauxhall model range took the top spot among on the Western European new car market for the fifth consecutive year.
The company had a 12.0 percent market share on unit sales that were up 2.1 percent to 1.54 million from 1995's 1.51 million vehicles in a total Western European car market of 12.8 million.
Opel/Vauxhall production rose 2.5 percent to a record 1.84 million vehicles.
Total GM group sales were 1.607 million vehicles, for an overall market share of 12.5 percent.
